sources.title: Democratizing access to large-scale language models with OPT-175B
sources.evidence: May 3, 2022 announcement names OPT-175B, 175 billion parameters, and a noncommercial research release; access to 175B requires a request, unlike the smaller downloadable models.

sources.title: OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models
sources.evidence: Table 1 specifies 96 layers, 96 heads and width 12288 for 175B; section 2.2 specifies 2048-token sequences. Appendix D identifies Meta AI, version 1.0.0, a decoder-only language model, and May 3, 2022 release. Section 2.4 distinguishes FP16 model weights from FP32 optimizer state.

sources.title: Applications of Meta’s OPT-175B: Protein design, quantum physics, translation, and more
sources.evidence: July 26, 2022 update confirms access granted to 668 entities. Requesters were manually screened before receiving weight-download links; initial access was gradually rolled out.

sources.title: OPT-175B License Agreement
sources.evidence: Section 1 grants use of the model software solely for non-commercial research; the repository code MIT license is separate from these model terms.

sources.title: OPT pretrained model weights
sources.evidence: Lists OPT-175B as a 175B member of Open Pre-trained Transformers and links to an access request; direct download links apply to smaller variants.

sources.title: Release-day OPT model-size configuration
sources.evidence: The exact 175b preset has 96 layers, width 12288, 96 heads, head width 128, eight-way tensor parallelism; FFN width is four times hidden width.

sources.title: Release-day OPT launcher
sources.evidence: Selects the size preset, 2048-token sequences, shared decoder input/output embedding and learned positions; no additional projection widths or optional scaling layers are selected.

sources.title: Release-day tensor-parallel language model
sources.evidence: Pads both dictionaries to a multiple of eight; the alternative padding to tensor-parallel-size times eight is commented out. Input/output dimensions default to hidden width and token embedding size comes from the loaded dictionary.

sources.title: Release-day Transformer decoder implementation
sources.evidence: Ties output-projection weight to token embedding without output bias; includes a final affine LayerNorm with pre-normalization. Equal embedding widths introduce no input/output projection matrices.

sources.title: Release-day Transformer layer implementation
sources.evidence: Defines two affine normalization layers per decoder block and two FFN projections. Optional additional normalization/scaling is conditional and absent from the released launcher preset.

sources.title: Release-day model-parallel attention implementation
sources.evidence: Defines full-width QKV and output projections with biases; tensor parallelism partitions the matrices rather than creating distinct model parameters for each shard.

sources.title: Release-day positional embedding implementation
sources.evidence: Learned positional embeddings allocate sequence length plus padding index plus one rows; padding index 1 therefore gives 2050 stored rows for a 2048-token context.

sources.title: Release-day OPT tokenizer vocabulary
sources.evidence: Fetched JSON contains 50265 token IDs, highest ID 50264, including pad ID 1; rounding this vocabulary to eight gives 50272 embedding rows.

sources.title: Release-day language-model dictionary loading
sources.evidence: The original language-model task loads its dictionary from external data/dict.txt. The tokenizer asset alone does not independently establish the gated checkpoint-associated dictionary and serialized configuration.

sources.title: Attempted official OPT-175B configuration
sources.evidence: Unauthenticated config request returned HTTP 401, as did the exact facebook/opt-175b model API request. This does not establish absence of a repository; no exact checkpoint config was inspected.

sources.title: 175B Training Run Completed
sources.evidence: The OPT-175B training chronicle explicitly calls this a dense model, independently supporting dense architecture rather than an inference from its name.

sources.title: Accessing OPT-175B
sources.evidence: Documents emailed presigned URLs and 992 model-parameter shard files across eight-way tensor parallelism, followed by consolidation. Weight download links require prior access approval.

sources.title: Release-day model-parallel FFN implementation
sources.evidence: Implements the two FFN matrices through column/row parallel linear layers with biases and no extra learned projection component.

name.note: Catalog spelling of the exact OPT-175B base model; not OPT-IML-175B or BlenderBot 3.

developer.note: Meta AI is the developing organization; Meta is the catalog developer name.

release_date.note: Appendix D explicitly assigns this release date. It marks the documented request-based research release, not unrestricted downloads. The announcement uses future-tense access grants; the first individual approval day is not established. The July update confirms actual grants, without redefining release as July.

open_weights.note: Weights were distributed to approved external researchers, with manual screening and presigned download links. True denotes weight availability under restrictions, not unrestricted access or an open-source license. Current fulfillment of new access requests was not tested.

license.note: Descriptive catalog label for the OPT-175B License Agreement; retain the non-commercial restriction.

parameters_b.note: 175B is the primary-source nominal size. Complete unique parameter-element reconciliation of the release-day reference configuration gives 174604468224 (174.604468224B): attention matrices 57982058496; FFN matrices 115964116992; projection biases 10616832; all affine norm weights/biases 4743168; tied token/output embedding 617742336; learned position tensor 25190400. Formula: 96*(4*h*h+2*h*f+9*h+f)+50272*h+2050*h+2*h, with h=12288 and f=49152. Count the shared embedding once, include the two reserved positional rows and padded vocabulary rows, and count tensor-parallel duplicates once. No optimizer state, masks, KV cache, quantization scales or storage padding are included; the original model uses FP16, not a quantized weight format. This is a reference-implementation reconstruction, not a checkpoint-header count: original loading uses external dict.txt and serialized checkpoint configuration, which were not inspected. Retain nominal 175 rather than substituting unjustified checkpoint-level precision. No full weight files were downloaded or unpickled.

active_parameters_b.note: No separately defined active-parameter count was found in the inspected primary sources. Dense architecture does not justify equating active and total parameters.

architecture.note: Explicitly dense in the OPT-175B training chronicle; decoder-only Transformer with 96 layers and 96 attention heads. No expert-routing architecture is substituted from another Meta model.

context_window.note: 2048 tokens in the paper and release-day launcher; the 2050-row position tensor includes two offset/reserved rows and does not imply a 2050-token context.

modalities.note: Language-model text input and generated text continuation are documented for this exact checkpoint. Research applications to proteins or other domains do not establish native image/audio input.

reasoning.note: Native reasoning-mode capability is not specified by the inspected model documentation. Benchmark results and ordinary prompted text generation do not resolve this catalog flag.

tool_call.note: Native structured tool/function calling is not documented for this checkpoint. Absence from these sources is not affirmative evidence of false.

description.note: The concise baseline description is supported; the accompanying notes clarify restricted weight access and nominal parameter precision.

patch.notes: Meta documents May 3, 2022 as the request-based OPT-175B research release; the first individual access-grant date is not established. Weights were distributed to approved researchers under non-commercial terms, with actual grants confirmed by July 26. The 175B size is nominal. Release-day reference code reconciles to 174.604468224B unique parameter elements, including tied embeddings, all biases/norms and 2050 position rows, but the original checkpoint-associated dictionary/configuration was not independently inspected; this is not an exact checkpoint-header count. Active parameters, native reasoning mode and native tool calling are not separately disclosed.

summary: Confirmed all supported baseline specifications and retained the primary nominal 175B total. Reconciled the original reference implementation to 174.604468224B unique parameter elements without claiming a verified gated-checkpoint count. Clarified May 3 as Meta’s documented request-based research release, with the first approval date unresolved and actual weight grants established by July. Active parameters and native reasoning/tool-calling flags remain undisclosed nulls.
